720	At the top, the connection between the head and the body is
721	the throat. The throat is
722	the connector: it joins the intellectual part with the
723	animal part, the physical part that man shares
724	with the beast, whose whole purpose is simply, technically,
725	to allow a person to exist. That is, thought, seemingly,
726	could exist only in the head, without the body. But then
727	a person could not bring thought out from potential
728	into actual and carry the thought out. So the carrying out
729	of thought is found in the organs of action, the organs of action
730	from the shoulders
731	down. Thought happens in the head. What happens in the connection?
732	Speech. The throat and the mouth, that is
733	speech. Speech is this
734	connection. The three actions, or three realms of
735	the possibility of
736	human action, and this is an idea that appears in Kabbalah many
737	times: the three fields of action are thought,
738	speech and deed. Deed is the deed done with the hands,
739	with the feet, action.
740	Speech is speech,
741	and thought: these are levels, one above
742	the other. Thought is where everything is found. That is to say,
743	thought is the most fantastic field and the most
744	exclusive, unique to man. Man is able
745	to think, able to understand, able
746	to think. Deed is something man shares with the animals.
747	Many of the deeds we do as human beings
748	we do on an instinctive level, like
749	animals. We are also able to do deliberate
750	deeds, meaning that the deed comes after
751	thought first. So there is thought and there is deed. What
752	does the throat connect?
753	Speech. Speech, then, is
754	an amazing tool, unique and exclusive to man. Only human beings
755	speak.
756	I mean intelligent speech. True, dolphins too
757	supposedly speak, and there is also the language of birds, but
758	that is chirping,
759	just sounds, not intelligent speech. Intelligent speech
760	is exclusive, unique to man, and the uniqueness
761	stems from the fact that only man has
762	a soul, a soul in the lofty
763	spiritual sense. Therefore the combination of body and soul is expressed
764	in speech. This is what gives speech
765	enormous importance, because, as we said, speech is
766	the garment of
767	thought. If we understand things
768	correctly, we can understand the commandment
769	in the Torah that one must keep
770	one's word: "That which has gone out of your lips you shall keep
771	and do." "He shall not profane his word." If a person says something and does not
772	fulfill it, this is called profaning the
773	word. Let us explain this expression for a moment. It appears, by the way,
774	in the book of Bamidbar, Parashat Matot, in the laws of vows: "If a man
775	vows a vow to HaShem, he shall not profane his word." What does
776	"shall not profane" mean? Speech that one does not fulfill is called
777	profaned. Let us explain the word "to profane." What
778	is
779	profanation? In the previous Parashah, Parashat Ki Tetzê,
780	we learned at the end of the Parashah, "If one is found
781	slain, fallen, and it is not known who struck him." What is a "challal"? Pity,
782	unfortunately we know this expression
783	all too well from the wars of Israel: "chalalim,"
784	fallen soldiers. Why is a person who died or
785	was killed called
786	a "challal"? It is also connected to the word
787	"chillul," profanation. Profanation is always the antithesis of
788	sanctification, kiddush.
789	Profaning the holy: Shabbat is
790	holy Shabbat. It is forbidden to profane Shabbat: "Those who profane it shall surely be put to death."
791	Chillul Shabbat. Why is it called profanation? The word chillul
792	is connected to the word
793	"challal," empty,
794	void. To profane is to take something that has content and remove
795	its content from it.
796	That is called
797	chillul. The people
798	of Israel: when the Holy One, blessed be He, chose us from all
799	the nations at Mount Sinai, He sent Moshe Rabbeinu
800	and offered us: "You shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy
801	nation." I always say jokingly that every Jew
802	is really a goy, only he must be a holy
803	goy. "You shall be holy, for I, HaShem, am holy." The people of
804	Israel is a people like all peoples, but it is holy; it has
805	holiness in it. The antithesis of
806	holiness is "chiloni," secular. By the way, this expression is a shocking
807	expression that we have all grown used to using, but
808	it is an expression that, for one who understands its meaning, people
809	speak without understanding what they are saying. What does it mean to be
810	a Jew
811	who is "chiloni"? Chiloni comes from the root of chillul. It is
812	the uprooting of holiness: I am a Jew but I do not
813	do anything holy. I do not do mitzvot,
814	"who has sanctified us with His commandments." I do not want to be sanctified
815	through His commandments, and I live my life as if I were not
816	a Jew. Now, if a non-Jew lives his life as a non-Jew,
817	fine, he is a goy. But a Jew has
818	an obligation to holiness. When he removes from within him
819	the holiness, he creates
820	a void, the chillul. So a person
821	who was killed, murdered, or from whom
822	his soul departed, a void is created, because the central, supreme,
823	spiritual thing that gives him life, "and He breathed into his nostrils the soul of
824	life," He gave a breath into them, a soul of life.
825	The soul gives life to the body, so when this soul
826	departs, a void is created. Therefore a person who fell in battle,
827	or in general
828	was murdered, not necessarily in battle, as the Torah says, "If one is found
829	slain, fallen in the field, and it is not known who," it does not have to
830	be someone who fell in battle: a person from whom
831	his central point has departed, which is
832	the soul. "He shall not profane his word": there is also such a thing. Speech
833	is holy. One who understands what we explained about
834	speech, that speech is the action of the holy soul
835	in the body. Now, once the soul acts in the body
836	and intelligent words come out, when a person knows
837	what he
838	committed himself to, it binds him. And if it does not bind
839	him, he, that is, if he does not stand by it, does not keep…
